title: Man. Post. Cap. X: PLAC — the fight is antecedent imputation: by what law, if any?
pass_a_gloss: But the question was antecedent or immediate imputation of Adam’s first actual sin to all his posterity—by what law? If by some law or denunciation, that law must have been violated; why then does the learned man ascribe that imputation everywhere to God’s free will?
pass_b_english: But the question was about the antecedent or immediate imputation of Adam’s first actual sin to all Adam’s posterity: according to what law does it take place?

If it takes place according to some law or denunciation of a law, it could not but be that that law was violated; why then does the learned man ascribe that imputation everywhere to the free will of God?
source_text: Sed quaerebatur de imputatione primi Adae peccati actualis antecedente seu immediata, omnibus Adae posteris, secundum quam legem fiat? Si fiat secundum aliquam legem seu legis denunciationem, non potuit non fieri quin lex illa violaretur; cur igitur eam imputationem Vir doctus liberae Dei voluntati ascribit passim?
